title: Knowledge Check 10 - Lessons 46-52
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 46-52 - Data Activations and Utilization. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: Which publish cadence option is available for a standard segment that must reach a destination frequently?
options: Real-time, on every event
Rapid publish at a shorter interval such as 1 or 4 hours
Dynamic, by API call
No schedule, membership updates instantly
questions.explanation: A standard segment can use rapid publish at shorter intervals on supported destinations; real-time is a segment type, and dynamic segments run by API call only.

questions.question: A business reports that a segment count fell sharply overnight with no rule change. Which explanation is most plausible?
options: The activation target was deleted
Existing members aged out of the lookback window, or an upstream identity resolution rerun consolidated duplicates
The segment type changed automatically
Segment membership is deleted every night by design
questions.explanation: Aging out of the lookback window and an upstream unification rerun that consolidates duplicates both lower the count; the platform does not change segment types or delete membership by design.

questions.question: A team cannot find a segment built by another team. What is the most likely cause?
options: The segment was automatically archived
The segment and its data are in a different data space, or the team lacks the needed permission set
Standard segments are private per user
Segments expire after 30 days
questions.explanation: Because a segment lives in a data space and requires the right permission set, a different space or a missing permission explains a segment that appears to be missing.

questions.question: A consultant needs to send an audience to an advertising platform such as Google Ads. What must be created first?
options: A calculated insight
An activation target that stores the platform authentication and authorization information
A real-time data graph
A Segment Membership data model object
questions.explanation: An activation target holds the credentials and configuration for the destination platform; external advertising platforms such as Google Ads and Meta are reached through an activation target.

questions.question: Which activation type cannot be published to an activation target?
options: Standard segment with standard publish
Standard segment with rapid publish
Dynamic segment
Waterfall segment
questions.explanation: Dynamic segments run by API call only, do not persist membership, and cannot be scheduled or published to activation targets; standard and waterfall segments can be published.

questions.question: An activation is saved against a segment that is still processing. How may it behave?
options: It publishes instantly regardless of segment state
It can remain in an error state until the segment finishes processing
It converts the segment to a standard segment
It deletes the segment
questions.explanation: Activating a segment that is still processing can leave the activation in an error state until the segment completes, so activate from an active or published segment.

questions.question: When is consent enforced for a Data 360 activation?
options: Only when the segment criteria are first saved
At activation time, using ingested and modeled consent preferences
Never, because consent is a CRM only concern
Only when the segment is a real-time segment
questions.explanation: Data 360 lets you ingest and model consent preferences, use them in segmentation, and check them at activation, so consent is enforced at activation time.

questions.question: An activation job reports success, but the marketing team sees no new audience. What is the most reliable next step?
options: Rebuild the segment from scratch
Verify the destination object such as the data extension or file, and compare the activation count to the segment count
Change the segment type to dynamic
Disable consent management
questions.explanation: A successful publish should be verified at the destination; a created data extension or file proves the pipeline end to end, and a large count gap points at contact point or consent filtering.

questions.question: What is the correct order when retiring an activation?
options: Delete the segment, then stop the activation
Pause or delete the activation, then handle the destination object, then adjust the segment schedule
Delete the destination object, then leave the activation running
Change the publish schedule to a real-time segment, then delete the target
questions.explanation: Stopping the activation first prevents further publishes, then the destination object is handled, and only then is the shared segment schedule adjusted, because other activations may rely on it.

questions.question: A business wants the service desk alerted within seconds when a unified profile's loyalty tier changes to the top tier. Which Data 360 feature fits?
options: An activation to an external platform
A data action with an event rule watching the loyalty DMO and an action rule on the tier value
A nightly data share to Snowflake
A copy field enrichment on the CRM record
questions.explanation: Data actions emit near real-time change events to a target when a DMO or CIO row changes and the action rule matches; activation sends whole segments on a schedule, and a share is for analytics access.

questions.question: Which statement about using Data 360 data in a flow is TRUE?
options: A flow can update a DMO directly with an Update Records element
A flow can read DMO and CIO data but cannot create, update, or delete Data 360 data
A flow can read raw data lake objects as well as DMOs
A flow must write the decision back to Data 360 before acting on a CRM record
questions.explanation: Flows read DMOs and calculated insight objects only; there is no DLO read and no Data 360 write, so the flow acts on CRM records instead.

questions.question: What distinguishes a data action from an enrichment write-back?
options: They are the same feature under two names
A data action emits a near real-time change event to a target, while an enrichment copies a harmonized value onto a CRM field or related list
Enrichment pushes the whole segment to Meta
A data action publishes only on a nightly schedule
questions.explanation: A data action is event-shaped and reactive to a DMO or CIO change; enrichment writes a value back inside the org onto a record field or related list.

questions.question: A marketing team needs a nightly audience pushed to an advertising platform. Which mechanism fits?
options: A data share to Snowflake
An activation that publishes the segment to an external platform activation target
A copy field enrichment on the CRM record
A data action to a webhook
questions.explanation: Activation publishes a segment to an external destination; a share is for analytics query access, enrichment is inline, and a data action is event-shaped rather than an audience push.

questions.question: A BI team needs direct query access to harmonized objects and calculated insights without loading copies into its warehouse. Which fits?
options: Activation to Marketing Cloud Engagement
A data share linked to a data share target
A data action to Amazon Kinesis
A related list enrichment on an account record
questions.explanation: Data shares (including zero copy sharing for Snowflake) expose DLOs, DMOs, and CIOs for external query without copying the data; the other options move audiences or events, not query access.

questions.question: A data share was created in Data 360, but the external Snowflake account cannot see it. What is the most likely cause?
options: The segment was never published
The data share is not linked to the data share target
The DMO has no records
The activation target is in draft state
questions.explanation: Until a data share is linked to a data share target it does not appear in the external system; publishing applies to segments, and record counts or DMO details do not gate visibility of a share.

questions.question: Which Flow element can retrieve Data 360 data, and how is it configured?
options: A Create Records element targeting a DMO
A Get Records element with its Data Source set to Data Cloud Object
An Update Records element targeting a DLO
A screen element bound to a calculated insight
questions.explanation: Get Records with the Data Cloud Object data source reads DMOs and CIOs; Create, Update, and Delete cannot write Data 360 data, and DLOs cannot be read.

questions.question: A developer adds a Get Records element that reads a DMO to the Run Immediately path of a record-triggered flow, and the element errors. What is the fix?
options: Change the object to a data lake object
Move the Data 360 read to a Run Asynchronously or scheduled path and optimize the flow for Actions and Related Records
Add Modify All Data to the running user
Remove the data space from the element
questions.explanation: Reads against Data Cloud objects must run on an asynchronous or scheduled path, so the read moves off the immediate transaction; the other options do not address the path constraint.

questions.question: What can a Data Cloud-triggered flow use as its start condition?
options: Only a change to a CRM Account
A DMO change or a calculated insight object result meeting a condition
A raw DLO insert event
A data share link event
questions.explanation: The Start element selects a Data Cloud object (a DMO or CIO) and conditions; for a DMO the object must be mapped as part of a data stream, and raw DLOs are not readable.

questions.question: A Data Cloud-triggered flow fires on an engagement-score threshold but creates a Lead with blank fields. What should you check first?
options: Whether the running user has Modify All Data
Whether the Get Records element found the harmonized profile row (correct data space and conditions) and handled the no-records outcome
Whether the raw DLO is accelerated
Whether the data share is linked to its target
questions.explanation: Blank fields usually mean the Data 360 read returned no row or the no-records path was taken; the data space and conditions of Get Records are the first thing to verify.

questions.question: After you activate a new Data Cloud-triggered flow, nothing happens in the test, but the logic looks correct. What should you check first?
options: Rewrite the Start condition from scratch
The data stream refresh history, since flow output depends on refresh and on timing
Recreate the Data 360 connection and redeploy
Convert the flow to a screen flow
questions.explanation: Data Cloud-triggered flow timing depends on the data stream refresh schedule, so a delay is expected; confirm the refresh before changing logic that already looks right.

questions.question: Which split keeps a Data 360 plus flow design trustworthy?
options: Read unified data in the flow, decide, then write the decision to the CRM record
Write the decision back to Data 360 with an Update Records element
Read the data lake object and update the DMO from the flow
Do everything on the Run Immediately path for speed
questions.explanation: Flows read Data 360 and cannot write it, so the decision is written to the CRM record; reading a DLO and writing to the Run Immediately path both violate the element limits.
